record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code and linked documents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports results from applying a rank-6 refusal-subspace weight edit to a released model, directly testing practical removal (V2), but not the original single-direction activation intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports refusal-related evaluation of the edited checkpoint and capability benchmark changes. The rank-6 configuration itself is stated, but results for alternative ranks or directions are not reported in the README. Runtime speed results and the safe-output KL statistic do not measure the refusal-removal behavior or general capability named by the versions, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The repo applies a refusal-subspace weight edit (rank 6, measured at layer 52, removed from attention-output and MLP down-projection weights in all 64 layers) to a released model. It reports refusal-related rates for the edited checkpoint, which bears on V2. The method differs from the original rank-1 difference-in-means ablation, and only aggregate post-edit numbers are given in the README.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors present the checkpoint as refusal-reduced, not refusal-free. They report zero opening refusal phrases but remaining soft refusals, call safe-output drift material, and warn that abliteration can damage normal behavior.
record.recipe_differences: The README describes a rank-6 refusal subspace reconstructed from the base model and a weight edit to attention output and MLP down-projection tensors across all 64 language layers. It does not report the original single-direction activation ablation or addition. Repository type: tool and model-release repository; it reports its own aggregate results.

fits_no_version.finding: After the rank-6 refusal-subspace weight edit, cyber and general-knowledge benchmarks change by at most 0.6 percentage points. The authors call the MMLU-Pro change inconclusive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A multi-rank refusal-subspace weight edit leaves multiple-choice capability benchmarks nearly unchanged.

record.problems: The README gives no unedited-base refusal rates or uncertainty estimates. Raw prompts and generations are excluded from the repository; the cited aggregate evaluation records were not available in the supplied text. Capability changes are reported without underlying scores, and MMLU-Pro is called inconclusive.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted from reported claim-relevant outcomes. Runtime throughput, safe-output KL, and repository file names are not outcomes for the tested refusal-removal version or a capability result.

untested.parts: Only one released model and one edit configuration are reported. No refusal rate for the unedited base is given in the README. Edits of other models and the original rank-1 weight orthogonalization are not reported.
A rank-6 subspace was released, but the README gives no comparison with rank-1. The docs file names suggest rank-1 trials, which were not read.
The single-direction activation ablation and the addition that induces refusal were not reported.

missing.what: Refusal and HarmBench rates of the unedited base model, needed to size the removal effect
Rank-1 direction results compared with the chosen rank-6 subspace, and layer-band screens
Safe first-token KL of 0.559 mean / 0.138 median over 192 prompts, described by the authors as material drift. This is a cost of the edit on harmless behavior.

record.verdict_notes: This is a hobbyist model-release repo, not peer reviewed, and only the README was available. All rows are post-edit values with no base comparison. The released rank-6 subspace and the many screening configs (rank1, rank2, bands) hint that a single direction was not judged sufficient, but this is not shown in the supplied text. The tranche could arguably be T3 (new model), but the edit method differs from the original, so T2 was kept.

versions.untested_parts: The README does not test the original single difference-in-means direction, activation projection at every layer and position, adding the direction to induce harmless refusals, or general abilities under that intervention.
Only one released edited model is reported. No direct refusal-rate comparison with its unedited base checkpoint is stated.
No attack mechanism or training against ablation is evaluated.
The README reports a rank-6 subspace but does not compare it with a single direction, affine geometry, a cone, or other directions.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision measures are reported.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer evaluation is reported.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or stages is reported.
No evaluation of reasoning models is reported.
